meta.title: Passive cooling and summer heat in social housing

primary.text: How does passive cooling change summer indoor temperatures and tenants' heat-related symptoms in social-housing blocks?
primary.scope: Social-housing blocks in three German cities, 2027 to 2030, with at least 20 rented dwellings per block.
primary.completion_criterion: The question is answered when peak indoor temperatures and reported symptoms are compared between retrofitted blocks and matched non-retrofitted blocks, before and after installation, with the uncertainty of both estimates reported.

secondary.text: Identify which building and household characteristics predict the largest reduction in indoor temperature.

method.approach: Quasi-experimental comparison of retrofitted and matched non-retrofitted blocks, with measurements before and after installation.

sources.description: Indoor temperature loggers in 60 social-housing blocks, three German cities, 2027-2030
Tenant health survey before and after each summer, 2027-2030
Building registers with construction year, orientation and rent level, 2026

method.procedure: Recruit 30 retrofitted and 30 matched blocks; install loggers in bedrooms and living rooms; collect readings at 15-minute intervals across two summers; survey tenants before and after each summer; estimate the difference in peak indoor temperature and symptom prevalence between retrofitted and matched blocks; test for pre-installation differences in the first summer.
validity_conditions: Retrofitted and comparison blocks are matched on construction year, orientation and rent level
Loggers are installed in the same rooms in every block
Tenants are surveyed in the summers before and after installation
limits: Findings cover the three participating cities, not the German building stock
The design measures indoor temperature, not the use of cooling systems
Households that move during the study leave the sample

results.claim: Passive cooling lowers peak indoor temperatures in retrofitted blocks by at least two degrees, and tenants report fewer heat-related symptoms.
results.falsifier: Peak indoor temperatures in retrofitted and matched blocks differ by less than half a degree, and the symptom survey shows no change.
results.evidence_needed: Logger readings for both summers and the symptom survey for every participating block.

results.claim: The number of summer nights above 26 degrees indoors, by block and bedroom.
results.measure: Logger readings aggregated to nights above the threshold, reported per bedroom and per block.

results.claim: A block-level dataset of temperature series and a retrofit audit protocol.

warrant.gap_statement: German building-stock models estimate energy savings from retrofit programmes but do not measure whether passive cooling lowers summer indoor temperatures in occupied social housing.
evidence: German Environment Agency, indoor heat and health in social housing, 2024
Federal Institute for Research on Building, Urban Affairs and Spatial Development, retrofit monitor, 2023
